mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stay near their current depressed levels for another month, weekday discretionary trips remain suppressed and RETAIL_REC will stay below its prior four-week average. The mechanism is a continuing commuter-traffic shortfall that reduces incidental shopping demand.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remaining at roughly the same depressed levels seen in the snapshot.

mechanism_narrative: A further drop in TRANSIT below its current trough will trigger fewer cross-district shopping trips within one week, causing RETAIL_REC to fall relative to the last four weeks. The causal claim fails if retail demand does not respond after transit weakens beyond that threshold.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 2 points below its current four-week average
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is around -30% in all four observed weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT crosses below the stated threshold but RETAIL_REC does not decline within the following week.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility stays elevated while WORKPLACES remain weak, more time is spent near home and discretionary purchases shift to non-retail channels, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks. The signal should strengthen if the home-stay pattern persists without a commuting rebound.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days even though RESIDENTIAL remains above zero and WORKPLACES stays near its current low level.

mechanism_narrative: Under a renewed tightening regime, restrained movement into TRANSIT and WORKPLACES transmits to lower shopping visits with a lag of about four weeks. If mobility restrictions intensify, RETAIL_REC should underperform its recent average; if restrictions do not tighten, the effect should disappear.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall another 3 points or more week-on-week
failure_condition: A further synchronized decline in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES is followed by no drop in RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS from its recent soft patch signals improving weather and outdoor activity, which can spill over into weekend shopping and lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The mechanism fails if park visits recover without any corresponding improvement in retail footfall.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above its current four-week mean
failure_condition: PARKS rises above the stated benchmark but RETAIL_REC stays flat or falls over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM declines while RETAIL_REC is already weak, households are not substituting toward brick-and-mortar errands but are reducing overall out-of-home activity, which will pull RETAIL_REC down over the next two weeks. The claim is falsified if grocery trips soften yet retail shopping improves.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -12% but RETAIL_REC does not decline within the following two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rebound in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicates more commuting-linked foot traffic, which should lift RETAIL_REC relative to the last four weeks over the next month. The effect should be strongest if both series rise together rather than one improving alone.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve but RETAIL_REC is not higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: If residential stay-at-home pressure eases and TRANSIT stabilizes rather than falls, the shift will release pent-up discretionary demand and RETAIL_REC will rise within one week. The mechanism fails when lower home-stay intensity does not translate into more retail visits.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below its current four-week average
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL drops below its recent average but RETAIL_REC does not increase within the next week.
